title: The two classical inputs of Stein connectedness
statement:
Let $(A,I)$ be a henselian pair [def-weil-pbc-henselian-terminology], let $p:Y\to S=\operatorname{Spec}A$ be proper [def-weil-proper-morphism], and put $Y_0=Y\times_S\operatorname{Spec}(A/I)$ [def-pc-fibre-product]. Write $Y\xrightarrow{q}\operatorname{Spec}B\xrightarrow{s}S$ for the Stein factorization [def-weil-pbc-stein-factorization], so $B=\Gamma(Y,\mathcal O_Y)$.

(i) The ring map $A\to B$ is integral. If, in addition, $A$ is Noetherian [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], then $B$ is a finite $A$-module and $s$ is finite [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism]; moreover $p_*\mathcal O_Y$ is coherent [pqf-def-coherent]. Finiteness is asserted only with this additional Noetherian hypothesis.

(ii) For every irreducible closed subset $C\subseteq Y$ [def-weil-irreducible-components], the intersection $C\cap |Y_0|$ is connected and nonempty [def-weil-connected-scheme], where the closed immersion $Y_0\to Y$ identifies $|Y_0|$ with $p^{-1}(V(I))$.

(iii) For every sheaf of sets $G$ on the underlying Zariski topological space of $Y$ (a presheaf satisfying unique gluing for every open cover), restriction induces a bijection $\Gamma(Y,G)\to\Gamma(Y_0,i^{-1}G)$, where $i:|Y_0|\hookrightarrow |Y|$ and $i^{-1}$ is the topological inverse image [def-weil-pbc-topological-inverse-image], with values in sets. Thus the comparison is available for the underlying Zariski sheaf of a constructible torsion sheaf as well; no local constancy hypothesis is needed.

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-stein-factorization-affine] to $p$. It gives that the induced $A\to B$ is integral, proving the general-base assertion in (i). Nothing here gives finiteness without a Noetherian hypothesis.

For the finite assertion only, assume $A$ Noetherian. The one affine chart $\operatorname{Spec}A$ makes $S$ locally Noetherian by [pqf-def-locnoeth]. Properness makes $p$ locally of finite type by [def-weil-proper-morphism], and [pqf-lem-locnoeth-lft] then makes $Y$ locally Noetherian. The structure sheaf is quasi-coherent of finite type: on an affine chart it is $\widetilde R$, and its identity map is a surjection from the rank-one free module to itself. Hence [pqf-lem-coherent-ft-locnoeth] makes $\mathcal O_Y$ coherent.

Apply [lem-pc-coherent-hi] to the proper $p$, the locally Noetherian $S$, and the coherent $\mathcal O_Y$ from Step 2. Its $i=0$ assertion gives coherence of $p_*\mathcal O_Y$, and its affine-base assertion gives finiteness of $H^0(Y,\mathcal O_Y)=B$ as an $A$-module. The affine morphism $s=\operatorname{Spec}(A\to B)$ is consequently finite by [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism]. This proves the remaining assertions of (i). The following steps require no Noetherian hypothesis.

The quotient morphism $\operatorname{Spec}(A/I)\to S$ is a closed immersion by [lem-weil-pbc-spec-quotient-closed-immersion]. Its base change $Y_0\to Y$ is a closed immersion by [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-base-change], hence a homeomorphism onto its closed image by [def-weil-closed-immersion]. That image is $p^{-1}(V(I))$: by [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-points] a point $y$ lies in the image exactly when a point $a_0\in\operatorname{Spec}(A/I)$ maps to $p(y)$ and their residue-field tensor product has a prime. The first condition says $I\subseteq p(y)$ by [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. In that case the residue field of $a_0$ is the residue field at $p(y)$, so the tensor product is $\kappa(y)$ and has the zero prime. Finally $p$ is separated and finite type by [def-weil-proper-morphism]; [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-over-affine] and [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-scheme-spectral] make $Y$ spectral.

proof.text: Fix an irreducible closed $C\subseteq Y$. By [lem-weil-pbc-closed-subset-closed-subscheme] choose a closed immersion $j:Z\to Y$ with image $C$. By [def-weil-closed-immersion], $j$ is a homeomorphism onto $C$, so $Z$ is irreducible and nonempty. By (c) and (a) of [lem-weil-pbc-proper-fp-permanence], $f=p\circ j$ is proper. It suffices to prove $f^{-1}(V(I))$ connected and nonempty: the homeomorphism $j$ carries this set onto $C\cap p^{-1}(V(I))=C\cap|Y_0|$.

source.place: Tag 0A0B, proof: replace X by an irreducible closed subscheme

proof.text: Use [def-weil-pbc-stein-factorization] for this proper $f$, writing $f=v\circ u$ with $u:Z\to\operatorname{Spec}D$, $D=\Gamma(Z,\mathcal O_Z)$ and $v=\operatorname{Spec}\varphi$ for $\varphi:A\to D$. By [lem-weil-pbc-stein-factorization-affine], $\varphi$ is integral, $u$ is proper, and each topological fibre $u^{-1}(d)$ is connected and nonempty. In particular $u$ is surjective. By [lem-weil-pbc-integral-over-henselian-pair], $(D,ID)$ is henselian.

proof.text: Use integral extension of henselian pairs to give (D,ID) a henselian structure, ID = I.map φ. Connectedness of Z means its global-section ring D has only the idempotents zero and one. Every idempotent in D/ID lifts to D by integral henselian idempotent lifting, so D/ID also has only zero and one. The Jacobson condition makes ID proper; hence Spec(D/ID) is connected and nonempty. Its continuous image is V(ID), which is therefore connected and nonempty. This route avoids importing proper-scheme idempotent lifting, whose proof already uses this connectedness result.

proof.text: The proper surjection $u$ is a closed map: proper means universally closed by [def-weil-proper-morphism], and we take base change along the identity. It is a quotient map, since if $u^{-1}(T)$ is closed then $T=u(u^{-1}(T))$ is closed; the converse holds by continuity. All fibres are connected by Step 6. The closed connected subset $V(ID)\subseteq\operatorname{Spec}D$ from Step 7 therefore has connected, nonempty inverse image by [lem-weil-pbc-connected-fibres-quotient-preimage-connected]. A prime $\mathfrak d\subseteq D$ belongs to $v^{-1}(V(I))$ iff $I\subseteq\varphi^{-1}(\mathfrak d)$ iff $ID\subseteq\mathfrak d$, so $v^{-1}(V(I))=V(ID)$, by [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. Consequently $u^{-1}(V(ID))=f^{-1}(V(I))$. Step 5 now proves (ii).

proof.text: For every $y\in Y$, the closed set $\overline{\{y\}}$ is irreducible: if it is covered by two relatively closed subsets, one contains $y$ and, being closed in its closure, contains all of $\overline{\{y\}}$. Apply (ii) to this closed irreducible subset. Step 4 supplies the other hypotheses, that $Y$ is spectral and $|Y_0|$ is closed. Thus [lem-weil-pbc-h0-spectral-closed-restriction], for the sheaf of sets $G$, gives exactly the bijection in (iii), with the topological inverse image and restriction unit described in [def-weil-pbc-topological-inverse-image]. There is no local constancy assumption in this criterion.
